questions.stem: What did Sarah think David was doing for the last two weeks?

options.B: He was recovering in hospital.
options.C: He was busy writing his essays.
options.D: He was fighting a throat infection.

questions.cn: 莎拉以为大卫过去两周在做什么？

questions.stem: What happened to David on his way back from the hospital?

options.B: He lost his antibiotics.
options.C: He slipped on ice and fell.
options.D: He was laughed at by some girls.

questions.cn: 从医院回来的路上，大卫发生了什么事？

questions.stem: What does Sarah say they should do with the damaged computer?

options.A: Turn to her father for help.
options.B: Call the repair shop to fix it.
options.C: Ask the manufacturer for repair.
options.D: Replace it with a brand-new one.

questions.cn: 关于那台摔坏的电脑，莎拉说他们该怎么做？

questions.stem: What does Sarah say she is going to do?

options.B: Introduce David to her parents.
options.C: Offer David some refreshments.
options.D: Accompany David to his home.

questions.cn: 莎拉说她要做什么？

lines.t: F: Hi David, I haven't seen you in class for almost two weeks.
lines.cn: F：嗨，大卫，我有快两周没在课上见到你了。

lines.t: F: We thought you had disappeared on holiday early or something.
lines.cn: F：我们还以为你提前去度假了什么的。

lines.t: M: Hi Sarah, well it's a bit of a long story I'm afraid.
lines.cn: M：嗨，莎拉，这事说起来话有点长。

lines.t: M: I got a throat infection last week and had to go to the hospital to get some antibiotics as I really wasn't getting any better.
lines.cn: M：我上星期得了咽喉感染，不得不去医院开抗生素，因为我一直不见好转。

lines.t: F: Oh yeah, there have been so many viruses going around this winter.
lines.cn: F：哦，是啊，今年冬天各种病毒太多了。

lines.t: F: The weather's been so awful for the last few weeks.
lines.cn: F：这几周天气也太糟糕了。

lines.t: M: And on the way back from the hospital I slipped on some ice and fell and then had to go to the hospital to get an x-ray because I basically thought I'd broken my wrist.
lines.cn: M：而且从医院回来的路上，我在冰上滑倒摔了一跤，然后又得去医院拍 X 光，因为我基本以为自己把手腕摔断了。

lines.t: M: Although thankfully it's not broken, but I need to be careful with it for the next few weeks.
lines.cn: M：幸好没断，但接下来几周我得小心着用。

lines.t: F: Oh that's too bad, how unfortunate.
lines.cn: F：哦，那太糟了，真不走运。

lines.t: M: To make things worse, I managed to fall right in front of four girls from the ninth grade, so I was utterly humiliated.
lines.cn: M：更糟的是，我恰好摔在九年级的四个女生面前，真是丢脸丢到底。

lines.t: M: Plus the laptop in my bag was broken too.
lines.cn: M：还有，我包里的笔记本电脑也摔坏了。

lines.t: F: Now what a complete catastrophe.
lines.cn: F：这可真是一场彻底的灾难。

lines.t: F: Is the laptop still under warranty?
lines.cn: F：那台笔记本还在保修期内吗？

lines.t: F: If it is, then you can easily send it back to the manufacturer and they'll send you a brand new one for free, surely.
lines.cn: F：如果在，你完全可以寄回给厂商，他们肯定会免费给你换个全新的吧。

lines.t: M: The warranty ran out three days before I broke it and all my essays are in there and I need to hand them in before we break for the Christmas holidays.
lines.cn: M：保修期在我摔坏它的三天前就到期了，而且我所有的论文都在里面，我得在放圣诞假之前交上去。

lines.t: F: Listen, I have the number of a really good affordable computer repair shop at home.
lines.cn: F：听着，我家里有一个特别靠谱、价格也合适的电脑维修店的电话。

lines.t: F: My dad has used this guy before and he can work miracles.
lines.cn: F：我爸以前找过这个人，他能创造奇迹。

lines.t: F: Let's go back to my house and we can call the repair shop and you can have some tea and cookies too.
lines.cn: F：我们回我家吧，可以给维修店打电话，你还能喝点茶、吃点饼干。

lines.t: M: Wow, thanks Sarah, that would be great.
lines.cn: M：哇，谢谢你莎拉，那太好了。

lines.t: M: Let me just call my mom and let her know I'll be home a little bit later.
lines.cn: M：我给我妈打个电话，告诉她我会晚点回家。

optionsCn.B: 它以 18 和 19 世纪为背景。

optionsCn.A: 她没有多少想象的自由。

lines.t: Conversation two.
lines.cn: 对话二。

lines.t: M: Welcome to this week's episode of Book Talk.
lines.cn: M：欢迎收听本周的《书谈》。

lines.t: M: With me today is Heidi Brown, a historian who has written five critically acclaimed books about military history.
lines.cn: M：今天和我一起的是海蒂·布朗，一位历史学家，写过五本广受好评的军事史著作。

lines.t: F: Thanks for having me, John.
lines.cn: F：谢谢你的邀请，约翰。

lines.t: F: I'm so excited to talk about my latest book, which was published last month.
lines.cn: F：我非常兴奋能谈谈我上个月出版的新书。

lines.t: M: So, this book is a novel, your first attempt at that genre, and thus a bit of a departure for you.
lines.cn: M：那么，这本书是一部小说，是你在这个体裁上的首次尝试，因此对你来说有点转向。

lines.t: F: I'd say it's a major departure, as it's not just a work of fiction.
lines.cn: F：我要说这是一次重大转向，因为它不只是一部虚构作品。

lines.t: F: It's set 200 years in the future.
lines.cn: F：它的背景设定在 200 年后的未来。

lines.t: M: Right, so how did that happen?
lines.cn: M：好，那这是怎么发生的呢？

lines.t: M: You spent three decades writing about the past and focusing on the 18th and 19th centuries, and now you're speculating about the future.
lines.cn: M：你花了三十年写过去，专注 18 和 19 世纪，如今却在推测未来。

lines.t: F: Well, after years of researching soldiers and chronicling their lives during battle, I just started wondering about other facets of their lives, especially their personal lives.
lines.cn: F：嗯，在研究士兵、记述他们战时生活多年之后，我开始好奇他们生活的其他方面，尤其是他们的私人生活。

lines.t: M: I can see that.
lines.cn: M：我明白。

lines.t: M: Your novel is about soldiers, but it focuses on their relationships, especially the bonds between sons and mothers and men and their wives.
lines.cn: M：你的小说写的是士兵，但聚焦于他们的关系，尤其是儿子与母亲、男人与妻子之间的纽带。

lines.t: F: Yes, that focus came about when I still intended to write another book of history.
lines.cn: F：是的，这个聚焦点是在我仍打算再写一本历史书的时候形成的。

lines.t: F: I started by researching soldiers' actual personal lives, studying their letters home.
lines.cn: F：我先研究士兵真实的私人生活，研读他们寄回家的信件。

lines.t: M: So, how did that history book become a novel?
lines.cn: M：那这本历史书怎么变成小说的呢？

lines.t: F: Well, I realized that the historical record was incomplete, so I'd either have to leave a lot of gaps or make a lot more assumptions than a historian should.
lines.cn: F：嗯，我意识到历史记录并不完整，所以我要么留下大量空白，要么得做出远比一位历史学家应该做的更多的假设。

lines.t: M: But why write a novel set in the future when your credentials are perfect for a historical novel?
lines.cn: M：但既然你的资历非常适合写历史小说，为什么要写一部设定在未来的小说？

lines.t: M: As a historian, any historical novel you write would have a lot of credibility.
lines.cn: M：作为历史学家，你写的任何历史小说都会很有可信度。

lines.t: F: I felt too constrained working with the past, like what I wrote needed to be fact as opposed to fiction.
lines.cn: F：我觉得和过去打交道太受限，好像我写的必须是事实而不是虚构。

lines.t: F: But writing about the future gave me more freedom to imagine, to invent.
lines.cn: F：而写未来给了我更多想象和创造的自由。

lines.t: M: Well, having read your book, I'm glad you made that choice to move into fiction.
lines.cn: M：嗯，读完你的书，我很高兴你做出了转向小说的选择。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the passage say appears in almost all ads for Coca-Cola?

options.B: Cocoa Seeds
options.C: A polar bear
options.D: A glass bottle

questions.cn: 文章说几乎每一则可口可乐广告里都会出现什么？

questions.stem: Why did the Coca-Cola company decide to have special packaging designed?

options.B: To keep up with the times.
options.C: To combat counterfeits.
options.D: To promote its sales.

questions.cn: 可口可乐公司为什么决定设计特殊的包装？

questions.stem: What do we learn about the Coca-Cola bottle designed by the Root Glass Company?

options.A: It resembles a picture in the encyclopedia.
options.B: It appears in the shape of a cocoa seed.
options.C: It has the drink's logo in the middle.
options.D: It displays the image of Santa Claus.

questions.cn: 关于鲁特玻璃公司设计的可口可乐瓶，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它像百科全书里的一幅图。
optionsCn.C: 它的中部有该饮料的标志。
optionsCn.D: 它展示圣诞老人的形象。

lines.t: Passage 1.
lines.cn: 短文一。

lines.t: Whether it's in the hands of animated polar bears or Santa Claus, there's one thing you'll find in nearly all ads for Coca-Cola, the characteristic glass bottle.
lines.cn: 无论是出现在动画北极熊手里，还是圣诞老人手里，你几乎在所有可口可乐广告里都能看到一样东西：那只标志性的玻璃瓶。

lines.t: Most Americans don't drink soda out of the glass bottles seen in Coke's ads anymore.
lines.cn: 大多数美国人已不再喝可乐广告里那种玻璃瓶装的汽水了。

lines.t: But this week, the company is celebrating a century of the bottle that's been sold in more than 200 countries.
lines.cn: 但本周，这家公司正在庆祝这种已在 200 多个国家销售的瓶子诞生一百周年。

lines.t: Flashback to 1915, when a bottle of Coca-Cola cost just a nickel.
lines.cn: 回溯到 1915 年，那时一瓶可口可乐只要五分钱。

lines.t: As the soft drink gained in popularity, it faced a growing number of competitors, counterfeits even trying to copy Coke's logo.
lines.cn: 随着这种软饮越来越受欢迎，它面临越来越多的竞争者，甚至有人仿制、试图抄袭可口可乐的标志。

lines.t: So according to Coca-Cola historian Ted Ryan, the company decided to come up with packaging that couldn't be duplicated.
lines.cn: 因此，据可口可乐历史学者泰德·瑞安说，公司决定设计一种无法被仿制的包装。

lines.t: A product request was sent to eight different glass makers.
lines.cn: 一份产品需求被发给了八家不同的玻璃制造商。

lines.t: Workers at the Root Glass Company got the request and began flipping through the encyclopedia at the local library, landing on cocoa seed.
lines.cn: 鲁特玻璃公司的工人接到需求后，开始翻阅当地图书馆的百科全书，最后翻到了可可豆。

lines.t: Though cocoa seed is not an ingredient of the soda, they designed their bottle based on the seed's shape and large middle.
lines.cn: 尽管可可豆并不是这种汽水的原料，他们还是依照可可豆的形状和宽大的中部设计了瓶身。

lines.t: It won over Coke executives in Atlanta and would go on to receive its own trademark, spur collections and earn Coca-Cola an iconic image that made it part of American culture for a century.
lines.cn: 它赢得了亚特兰大可口可乐高管的认可，后来还获得了自己的商标，引发了收藏热，并为可口可乐赢得了一个使它成为美国文化一部分达一个世纪之久的标志性形象。

lines.t: It was 100 years ago this week that the bottle earned a patent.
lines.cn: 就在本周，这只瓶子获得专利满 100 年。

lines.t: By World War II, Coke bottle sales had ballooned into billions.
lines.cn: 到二战时，可乐瓶的销量已激增至数十亿。

lines.t: Americans mostly consume Coke out of aluminum or plastic today, but the glass bottle remains a symbol of America that's readily recognized around the world.
lines.cn: 如今美国人喝的多数是铝罐或塑料瓶装可乐，但玻璃瓶依然是美国的一个象征，为全世界所熟知。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does research show about a conversation between strangers?

options.B: It promotes mutual understanding.
options.C: It improves their mood considerably.
options.D: It takes a great deal of effort to sustain.

questions.cn: 关于陌生人之间的交谈，研究显示了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它常发生在通勤者之间。
optionsCn.C: 它大大改善他们的情绪。

questions.stem: What prevents people from starting a conversation with strangers?

options.B: Excessive caution.
options.C: Lack of social skills.
options.D: Preference for solitude.

questions.cn: 是什么妨碍人们主动与陌生人交谈？

questions.stem: Why does a negative encounter with strangers stick in one's memory?

options.A: People usually regard it as an unforgettable lesson.
options.B: Human brains tend to dwell on negative events.
options.C: Negative events often hurt people deeply.
options.D: People generally resent being rejected.

questions.cn: 为什么一次与陌生人的负面经历会留在记忆中？

optionsCn.A: 人们通常把它当作难忘的一课。
optionsCn.B: 人脑倾向于纠结负面事件。
optionsCn.C: 负面事件往往深深伤害人。

questions.stem: What does the passage say the pleasure of connection seems to be?

options.B: Temporary.
options.C: Unpredictable.
options.D: Measurable.

questions.cn: 文章说连接的愉悦似乎是怎样的？

lines.t: Passage 2.
lines.cn: 短文二。

lines.t: Research shows that a few moments of conversation with a stranger creates a measurable improvement in mood, but most of us are reluctant to start these conversations because we presume the opposite.
lines.cn: 研究显示，与陌生人交谈片刻就能显著改善情绪，但我们大多数人都不愿开启这类对话，因为我们预设的结果正好相反。

lines.t: In an experiment, commuters who talked to nearby strangers found their commute more enjoyable than those who didn't.
lines.cn: 在一项实验中，与附近陌生人交谈的通勤者，比不交谈的人觉得通勤更愉快。

lines.t: They were asked to predict whether they'd enjoy the commute more if they conversed with other people.
lines.cn: 他们被要求预测：如果和别人交谈，自己是否会觉得通勤更愉快。

lines.t: Intriguingly, most expected the more solitary experience to be more pleasurable.
lines.cn: 有趣的是，大多数人预期更孤独的体验会更令人愉快。

lines.t: Why is this?
lines.cn: 为什么会这样？

lines.t: Social anxiety appears to be the problem.
lines.cn: 社交焦虑似乎是问题所在。

lines.t: People's reluctance to start conversations with nearby strangers comes partly from underestimating others' interest in connecting.
lines.cn: 人们不愿与附近的陌生人开启对话，部分原因在于低估了他人建立联系的兴趣。

lines.t: The sad thing is that people presume that a nearby stranger doesn't want to converse and don't start a conversation.
lines.cn: 令人遗憾的是，人们预设附近的陌生人不想交谈，于是不去开启对话。

lines.t: Only those who forced themselves to chat because it was required by the experiment found out what a pleasant experience it could be.
lines.cn: 只有那些因为实验要求而强迫自己去聊天的人，才发现那可以是多么愉快的经历。

lines.t: Human beings are social animals.
lines.cn: 人类是社交动物。

lines.t: Those who misunderstand the impact of social interactions may not.
lines.cn: 那些误解社交互动影响的人，可能就不会那么社交。

lines.t: In some contexts, be social enough for their own well-being.
lines.cn: 在某些情境中，社交程度足以有益于自身幸福。

lines.t: You should be chatting with the strangers you encounter.
lines.cn: 你该和遇到的陌生人聊聊天。

lines.t: You may occasionally have a negative encounter that might stick in your memory.
lines.cn: 你偶尔可能遇到一次负面经历，它也许会在你记忆里停留很久。

lines.t: This is because the human brain is biased to dwell on negative events.
lines.cn: 这是因为人脑倾向于纠结于负面事件。

lines.t: But starting conversations with strangers is still well worth the risk of rejection.
lines.cn: 但和陌生人开启对话仍然非常值得冒被拒绝的风险。

lines.t: It may surprise you that conversing with strangers will make them happier too.
lines.cn: 也许会让你吃惊的是，与陌生人交谈也会让他们更快乐。

lines.t: The pleasure of connection seems contagious.
lines.cn: 连接的愉悦似乎具有传染性。

lines.t: People who are talked to have equally positive experiences as those who initiate a conversation.
lines.cn: 被别人搭话的人和主动开启对话的人有着同样积极的体验。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 1 组

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the economy of the Caribbean islands?

options.B: It is flourishing in foreign trade.
options.C: It is mainly based on agriculture.
options.D: It relies chiefly on mineral export.

questions.cn: 关于加勒比群岛的经济，讲话者说了什么？

questions.stem: What is the main product of the Caribbean islands?

options.B: Bananas.
options.C: Coffee.
options.D: Sugar.

questions.cn: 加勒比群岛的主要产品是什么？

questions.stem: What do we learn about the majority of people in the Caribbean islands?

options.B: They live a poor life.
options.C: They live in Spanish-style houses.
options.D: They hire people to do housework.

questions.cn: 关于加勒比群岛的大多数人，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.C: 他们住在西班牙式宅邸里。

lines.t: Recording 1.
lines.cn: 录音一。

lines.t: The Caribbean islands are divided into two worlds.
lines.cn: 加勒比群岛分为两个世界。

lines.t: A rich one and a poor one.
lines.cn: 一个富裕的世界，一个贫穷的世界。

lines.t: This tropical region's economy is based mainly on farming.
lines.cn: 这个热带地区的经济主要以农业为基础。

lines.t: Farmers are of two types.
lines.cn: 农民有两类。

lines.t: One is the plantation owner who may have hundreds of thousands of acres.
lines.cn: 一类是可能拥有数十万英亩土地的种植园主。

lines.t: In contrast, the small cultivator is working only a few acres of land.
lines.cn: 相比之下，小农只耕种几英亩土地。

lines.t: Most visitors to the Caribbean are rich.
lines.cn: 到加勒比的大多数游客都是有钱人。

lines.t: Like the plantation owner, they do not realize or do not want to realize that many farm families barely manage to get by on what they grow.
lines.cn: 和种植园主一样，他们没有意识到、或者不愿意识到，许多农家靠种出来的东西勉强糊口。

lines.t: The Caribbean produces many things.
lines.cn: 加勒比出产很多东西。

lines.t: Sugar is the main product.
lines.cn: 糖是主要产品。

lines.t: Other export crops are tobacco, coffee, bananas, spices, and citrus fruits, such as orange, lemon, or grapefruit.
lines.cn: 其他出口作物有烟草、咖啡、香蕉、香料以及柑橘类水果，如橙子、柠檬或葡萄柚。

lines.t: From the West Indies also come oil, mineral pitch, and many forest products.
lines.cn: 西印度群岛还出产石油、沥青以及许多林产品。

lines.t: Jamaica's aluminum ore supplies are the world's largest.
lines.cn: 牙买加的铝矿储量居世界首位。

lines.t: Oil comes from Trinidad, Aruba, and Caraco.
lines.cn: 石油来自特立尼达、阿鲁巴和库拉索。

lines.t: But for many of the smaller islands, sugar is the only export.
lines.cn: 但对许多较小的岛屿来说，糖是唯一的出口品。

lines.t: Rum, a strong alcoholic drink, which is distilled from sugar cane, is also an export.
lines.cn: 朗姆酒——一种从甘蔗蒸馏出的烈性酒——也是一种出口产品。

lines.t: The world's best rum comes from this area.
lines.cn: 世界上最好的朗姆酒就产自这一地区。

lines.t: Local kinds vary, from the light rums of Puerto Rico to the heavier, darker rums of Barbados and Jamaica.
lines.cn: 各地品种不同，从波多黎各的清淡朗姆酒，到巴巴多斯和牙买加更浓更深的朗姆酒。

lines.t: American tourists enjoy stocking up on inexpensive, high-quality Caribbean rum while they are on vacation.
lines.cn: 美国游客喜欢在度假时囤些价廉质优的加勒比朗姆酒。

lines.t: In Caraco, the well-known liquor of that name is made from the thick outer skin of a native orange.
lines.cn: 在库拉索，那款著名同名利口酒是用当地一种橙子的厚外皮酿成的。

lines.t: Ever since America's colonial days, the Caribbean islands have been favorite places to visit.
lines.cn: 自美国殖民时代以来，加勒比群岛一直是人们喜爱的旅行地。

lines.t: Since World War II, tourism has increased rapidly.
lines.cn: 二战以来，旅游业迅速增长。

lines.t: Because great numbers of people go there, the islanders have built elaborate resorts, developed harbors and airfields, improved beaches, and have expanded sea and air routes.
lines.cn: 由于大量人前往，岛民修建了精致的度假村，开辟了港口和机场，改善了海滩，并扩展了海空航线。

lines.t: Everything is at the resort.
lines.cn: 度假村里什么都有。

lines.t: Hotel, beach, shopping, and recreation.
lines.cn: 酒店、海滩、购物和娱乐。

lines.t: The vacationer never has any reason to explore the island.
lines.cn: 度假者从来没有任何理由去探索这座岛。

lines.t: As in most places, those who have money live well indeed.
lines.cn: 和大多数地方一样，有钱人确实过得很好。

lines.t: Those who don't have money live at various levels of poverty.
lines.cn: 没钱的人则生活在不同程度的贫困中。

lines.t: But here, the poor greatly outnumber the wealthy.
lines.cn: 但在这里，穷人远远多于富人。

lines.t: A visitor will find rich people living in apartments or Spanish houses at the seaside or in the countryside.
lines.cn: 游客会看到富人住在海边或乡间的公寓或西班牙式宅邸里。

lines.t: Their servants might include a cook, a maid, and a nurse for the children.
lines.cn: 他们的仆人中可能有厨师、女佣和照看孩子的保姆。

lines.t: Most of the people live well below the poverty level.
lines.cn: 大多数人生活在贫困线以下很多。

lines.t: In towns, they live crowded together in tiny houses.
lines.cn: 在城里，他们挤在狭小的房子里。

lines.t: Islanders make the best they can of what they have.
lines.cn: 岛民们尽力把所拥有的东西用好。

lines.t: Their homes are quite shabby.
lines.cn: 他们的家相当破旧。

lines.t: Sadly, most tourists never see this side of the Caribbean.
lines.cn: 遗憾的是，大多数游客从未见过加勒比的这一面。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What will happen to children if they always get immediate satisfaction?

options.A: They will be more demanding of their next generation.
options.B: They will end up lonely, dependent and dissatisfied.
options.C: They will experience more setbacks than successes.
options.D: They will find it difficult to get along with others.

questions.cn: 如果孩子总能立刻得到满足，会怎样？

optionsCn.A: 他们对下一代要求更多。
optionsCn.B: 他们最终孤独、依赖、不满足。
optionsCn.C: 他们经历的挫折多于成功。
optionsCn.D: 他们发现难以与人相处。

questions.stem: What may prevent parents from raising confident and capable children?

options.A: Failure to pay due attention to their behavior.
options.B: Unwillingness to allow them to play with toys.
options.C: Unwillingness to satisfy their wishes immediately.
options.D: Failure to spend sufficient quality time with them.

questions.cn: 什么可能妨碍父母养育出自信能干的孩子？

optionsCn.A: 未能适当关注他们的行为。
optionsCn.C: 不愿立刻满足他们的愿望。
optionsCn.D: 未能与他们共度足够的高质量时间。

questions.stem: Why should children be encouraged to keep trying when they fail?

options.A: It will enable them to learn from mistakes.
options.B: It will help them to handle disappointment.
options.C: It will do much good to their mental health.
options.D: It will build their ability to endure hardships.

questions.cn: 孩子失败时为什么应被鼓励继续尝试？

optionsCn.A: 这会让他们从错误中学习。
optionsCn.C: 这对其心理健康大有好处。
optionsCn.D: 这会培养他们忍受艰难的能力。

lines.t: Recording 2.
lines.cn: 录音二。

lines.t: Talk to anyone who is a generation or two older, and they would most likely comment that children are more spoiled these days.
lines.cn: 跟大一两代的人聊一聊，他们多半会说如今的孩子被宠坏了。

lines.t: No one wants to have or be around demanding, selfish, and spoiled children.
lines.cn: 没有人愿意拥有或待在要求多、自私、被宠坏的孩子身边。

lines.t: Those who get bad-tempered or silently brood when they're not given everything they want immediately.
lines.cn: 那些没立刻得到想要的一切就发脾气或默默记恨的孩子。

lines.t: Paradoxically, the parents of such children encourage this demanding behavior in the mistaken belief that by giving their children everything they can, their children will be happy.
lines.cn: 矛盾的是，这类孩子的父母却在助长这种索求行为，误以为只要把能给的都给孩子，孩子就会幸福。

lines.t: In the short term, perhaps they are right.
lines.cn: 短期看，也许他们是对的。

lines.t: But in the longer term, such children end up lonely, dependent, chronically dissatisfied, and resentful of the parents who tried so hard to please them.
lines.cn: 但长期看，这样的孩子最终会孤独、依赖、长期不满，并怨恨那些竭力讨好他们的父母。

lines.t: Undoubtedly, parents want to raise happy children who are confident, capable, and likable rather than spoiled and miserable.
lines.cn: 无疑，父母都想养育出自信、能干、讨人喜欢而不是被宠坏、痛苦的孩子。

lines.t: One factor hindering this is that parents can't or don't spend enough quality time with their kids and substitute this deficit with toys, games, gadgets, and the like.
lines.cn: 妨碍这一点的一个因素是，父母不能或没有花足够的高质量时间陪伴孩子，于是用玩具、游戏、电子产品之类来弥补这种缺失。

lines.t: Rather than getting material things, children need parents' devoted attention.
lines.cn: 孩子需要的不是物质的东西，而是父母专注的陪伴。

lines.t: The quantity of time spent together is less important than the content of that time.
lines.cn: 共处时间的长短，不如这段时间的内容重要。

lines.t: Instead of instantly satisfying their wishes, parents should help them work out a plan to earn things they'd like to have.
lines.cn: 父母不应立刻满足孩子的愿望，而应帮他们制定计划，靠努力去挣得想要的东西。

lines.t: This teaches them to value their effort as well as what it achieves.
lines.cn: 这教会他们看重自己的努力以及努力所取得的成果。

lines.t: Allow them to enjoy anticipation.
lines.cn: 让他们享受期待的过程。

lines.t: Numerous psychological studies have demonstrated that children who learn to wait for things they desire are more likely to succeed in a number of ways later in life.
lines.cn: 大量心理学研究表明，学会等待自己想要之物的孩子，日后在多个方面更可能成功。

lines.t: One famous experiment in the 1960s involved three to six-year-old children.
lines.cn: 1960 年代一项著名实验以 3 至 6 岁的孩子为对象。

lines.t: They were given a choice between receiving a small reward, such as a cookie, immediately, or if they waited 15 minutes, they could have two.
lines.cn: 他们可以选择立刻得到一份小奖励（比如一块饼干），或者等待 15 分钟得到两块。

lines.t: Follow-up studies have found that those who chose to delay satisfaction are now more academically successful, have greater self-worth, and even tend to be healthier.
lines.cn: 后续研究发现，那些选择延迟满足的孩子如今学业更成功、自我价值感更强，甚至往往更健康。

lines.t: If they fail, children should be encouraged to keep trying rather than to give up if they really want the desired result.
lines.cn: 如果失败了，只要他们真的想要那个结果，就应鼓励孩子继续尝试而不是放弃。

lines.t: This teaches them how to handle and recover from disappointment, which is associated with greater success and satisfaction academically, financially, and in personal relationships.
lines.cn: 这教会他们如何应对失望、从失望中恢复，而这与学业、财务和人际关系上更大的成功与满足感相关联。

lines.t: And lastly, parents should encourage their children to look at life from other points of view as well as their own.
lines.cn: 最后，父母应鼓励孩子从他人的角度、而不只是自己的角度看生活。

lines.t: This teaches them to be understanding of and sympathetic towards others, qualities sure to take them a long way in life.
lines.cn: 这教会他们体谅和同情他人，这些品质必将让他们受益终身。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say can easily prevent an interviewee from getting a job?

options.B: Looking away from the hiring manager.
options.C: Saying the wrong thing at the wrong time.
options.D: Making a wrong judgment of the interview.

questions.cn: 讲话者说什么很容易让求职者得不到工作？

questions.stem: What should the interviewee avoid doing in an interview?

options.B: Inquiring about their salary to be paid.
options.C: Exaggerating their academic background.
options.D: Understanding their previous achievements.

questions.cn: 面试中求职者应避免做什么？

questions.stem: What kind of employees do companies like to recruit?

options.A: Those who have both skill and experience.
options.B: Those who get along well with colleagues.
options.C: Those who take initiative in their work.
options.D: Those who are loyal to their managers.

questions.cn: 公司喜欢招什么样的员工？

optionsCn.A: 既有技能又有经验的人。
optionsCn.C: 在工作中主动作为的人。

questions.stem: What is especially important for those working in a small company?

options.B: Experience of performing multiple roles.
options.C: Readiness to work to flexible schedules.
options.D: Skills to communicate with colleagues.

questions.cn: 对小公司里的员工来说，什么尤其重要？

optionsCn.C: 愿意弹性安排工作时间。

lines.t: Recording 3.
lines.cn: 录音三。

lines.t: It's not hard to mess up an interview.
lines.cn: 把面试搞砸并不难。

lines.t: Most people feel nervous sitting across from a hiring manager, answering questions that effectively open themselves up for judgment.
lines.cn: 大多数人坐在招聘经理对面、回答那些把自己交由对方评判的问题时都会紧张。

lines.t: And your chances of being more carefully considered for the job can quickly go downhill just by saying the wrong thing at the wrong time.
lines.cn: 而在错误的时机说错话，会让你被认真考虑录用的机会迅速下降。

lines.t: The most obvious thing not to do is complain.
lines.cn: 最明显不该做的事就是抱怨。

lines.t: Employers want to hire positive people.
lines.cn: 雇主想招的是积极的人。

lines.t: Talking about a previous job negatively raises concerns that you might be difficult to manage, or you might be someone that blames management for your own poor performance.
lines.cn: 负面评价前一份工作，会让人担心你可能难以管理，或者会把自身表现不佳归咎于管理层。

lines.t: Don't say that you've moved around in jobs because you haven't found the right fit or feel that you were not challenged enough.
lines.cn: 不要说你在不同工作间换来换去，是因为没找到合适的位置，或者觉得没受到足够挑战。

lines.t: Statements like these will make you sound aimless and lost.
lines.cn: 这类说法会让你听起来没有方向、漫无目标。

lines.t: An interviewer may well think, why would this role be any different for you?
lines.cn: 面试官很可能想：这个岗位对你来说凭什么就会不同呢？

lines.t: You will probably leave here in six months.
lines.cn: 你大概六个月后就会走人。

lines.t: It also begs the question of what type of relationship you had with your manager.
lines.cn: 这还会引出另一个问题：你和你的经理曾是什么关系？

lines.t: It doesn't sound like you had open communication with him or her.
lines.cn: 听起来你和他/她之间并没有开诚布公的沟通。

lines.t: Managers usually love people who can self-sustain and enable growth through taking initiative, who are strong at following through their work, and who bring ideas and solutions to the table.
lines.cn: 管理者通常喜欢能自我驱动、通过主动作为带来成长的人，喜欢能坚持把工作做完的人，以及能把想法和方案摆上桌面的人。

lines.t: If you were in a management or leadership position, when discussing your current role, never take all the credit for accomplishments or achievements.
lines.cn: 如果你身处管理或领导岗位，谈到当前职位时，绝不要把功劳全部归于自己。

lines.t: Emphasize your team and how through their talents, your vision was realized.
lines.cn: 要强调你的团队，以及如何借助他们的才能实现了你的构想。

lines.t: Most successful leaders know that they are only as good as their team.
lines.cn: 大多数成功的领导者都知道，自己有多大本事取决于自己的团队。

lines.t: And acknowledging this in an interview will go a long way towards suggesting that you might be the right person for the position you are applying for.
lines.cn: 在面试中承认这一点，会大大有助于表明你可能是所申请职位的合适人选。

lines.t: Lastly, have a good idea of what your role will be and try and convey the idea that you're flexible.
lines.cn: 最后，要清楚了解你的岗位职责，并设法传达出你很灵活的印象。

lines.t: Asking what your role will be suggests you will limit yourself purely to what is expected of you.
lines.cn: 问“我的职责是什么”，会让人觉得你只把自己限于别人要求你做的事。

lines.t: In reality, your role is whatever you make of it.
lines.cn: 实际上，你的职责是你自己去塑造的。

lines.t: This is especially true in small companies, where the ability to adapt and take on new responsibilities is highly valued.
lines.cn: 在小公司尤其如此，那里高度看重适应能力和承担新职责的能力。

lines.t: And this is equally important if you're just starting out.
lines.cn: 如果你是刚起步，这一点同样重要。

lines.t: Entry-level interviewees would do well to demonstrate a broad set of skills in most interviews.
lines.cn: 入门级求职者在多数面试中，展示一套广泛的技能会很有帮助。

lines.t: It's important to have a wide skill set.
lines.cn: 拥有广泛的技能组合很重要。

lines.t: As many startups and small companies are moving really fast, employers are looking for candidates that are intelligent and can quickly adapt and excel in a growing company.
lines.cn: 由于许多初创公司和小公司发展极快，雇主在寻找聪明、能快速适应并在成长型公司中脱颖而出的求职者。
